    At most three arrows start at a point #

    In a ray category over which a minimal representation-infinite algebra has a twisted multiplicative basis, and which has a non-irreducible non-invertible nonzero morphism, at most three irreducible morphisms start at any object (RayQuiver.MulBasis.not_four_irr; used in BO13a Lemmas 5 and 6).

    f = g

    Two irreducible morphisms out of x, one a prefix of the other, agree.

    At most three irreducible morphisms start at an object.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.RayQuiver.MulBasis.not_contours_out {P : Type} [CategoryTheory.Category.{0, 0} P] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms P] [IsRayCategory P] [Fintype P] [DecidableEq P] [IsFiniteRayCategory P] {k : Type u} [Field k] [Infinite k] {A : Type u} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] (B : MulBasis k P A) (hmin : ∀ (I : TwoSidedIdeal A), I ≠ ⊥ → Statement.IsRepresentationFinite (A ⧸ TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I)) (hL : RayCat.LeftCancel P) (hR : RayCat.RightCancel P) {x a b y a' b' y' : RayCat.RayVert P} (α : x ⟶ a) (β : x ⟶ b) (v' : Quiver.Path a y) (w' : Quiver.Path b y) (hval : RayCat.pathVal (α.toPath.comp v') = RayCat.pathVal (β.toPath.comp w')) (h0 : RayCat.pathVal (α.toPath.comp v') ≠ 0) (hni : ¬RayCat.Interlaced (α.toPath.comp v') (β.toPath.comp w')) (hτ : ¬CategoryTheory.IsIso (RayCat.pathVal (α.toPath.comp v'))) (hτr : ¬IsIrreducible (RayCat.pathVal (α.toPath.comp v'))) (α' : x ⟶ a') (β' : x ⟶ b') (v'' : Quiver.Path a' y') (w'' : Quiver.Path b' y') (hval' : RayCat.pathVal (α'.toPath.comp v'') = RayCat.pathVal (β'.toPath.comp w'')) (h0' : RayCat.pathVal (α'.toPath.comp v'') ≠ 0) (hni' : ¬RayCat.Interlaced (α'.toPath.comp v'') (β'.toPath.comp w'')) (hα : ¬RayCat.BLe (RayCat.arrB α) ⟨y'.out, RayCat.pathVal (α'.toPath.comp v'')⟩) (hβ : ¬RayCat.BLe (RayCat.arrB β) ⟨y'.out, RayCat.pathVal (α'.toPath.comp v'')⟩) :
    False

    BO13a Lemma 5 a), first case. Let σ = val(α v') = val(β w') and ρ = val(α' v'') = val(β' w'') be morphisms out of x from two contours. If ρ factors through neither α nor β, the four first arrows give four irreducible morphisms out of x, which is impossible.
